## Abstract

Accurate progesterone receptor (PR) status is a critical
determinant of endocrine therapy eligibility in breast cancer,
yet standard immunohistochemistry (IHC) exhibits substantial
inter-pathologist variability in diagnostically ambiguous cases.
We present a multimodal clinical decision-support system that
integrates RNA-Seq transcriptomic profiles with whole-slide
imaging (WSI) to improve PR status prediction. To address the
mismatch between molecular profiles and variable-length WSI
representations, we introduce an asymmetric cross-attention
mechanism in which the patient's transcriptomic profile guides
visual evidence retrieval from the tissue image with linear
computational complexity. A Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator
provides a calibrated per-patient confidence score to identify
cases requiring additional pathologist review. A
normalization-corrected Top-1%-Mass Concentration metric
quantifies attentional focus consistently across slides of
any size.

Using the TCGA-BRCA cohort of 951 patients with matched molecular
and imaging data, the model achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.8482 and
PR-AUC of 0.9054. The reliability estimator produces a
statistically robust per-patient confidence score, enabling
automated escalation of discordant cases to pathologist review.
Analysis of attention patterns revealed significant phenotypic
separation between PR-positive and PR-negative tumors (p = 0.018),
confirming the model captures spatial patterns associated with
PR phenotype.

Together, these findings demonstrate that genomic-conditioned
visual search is an effective framework for multimodal
computational pathology. The results further show that the
measurement instrument, not the model, determines whether
biological signal is recoverable.

## Key Contributions

::: {.callout-note}
## Asymmetric Cross-Attention Fusion
Treats the patient's transcriptomic profile as a query token
that searches the entire slide for diagnostically relevant
tissue at linear computational cost, without positional
encoding, pathway annotation, or pre-aggregation.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator
A lightweight gated fusion layer producing a per-patient
confidence score reflecting cross-modal agreement between
genomic and imaging evidence. Cases where the two streams
disagree are flagged for pathologist review rather than
issued a high-confidence binary prediction.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Top-1%-Mass Concentration
A normalization-independent interpretability metric that
quantifies attentional focus consistently across any slide
size, recovering statistically significant phenotypic
separation that entropy-based analysis fails to recover
on the same cohort.
:::
